Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice M.Nagaprasanna
 Oral Order

The petitioners in Crl.P.No.6542/2019 are before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime No.36/2019, pending before the 43rd Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Mayo Hall, Bengaluru, registered for the offences under Sections 498A r/w. 149 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

entities.text:
43rd Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Mayo Hall, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner - husband in Crl.P.No.7057/2022 is calling in NC: 2024:KHC:36744 question proceedings in C.C.No.2166/2022,
pending before the 41st Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, for the offences under Sections 323 and 354B of the IPC.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 in both the petitions, in unison would submit that the parties to the lis were before the concerned family Court in M.C.No.2394/2020 and have settled their dispute among themselves amicably before the Mediation Center.
The parties to the lis have decided to obtain a decree of divorce by mutual consent before the concerned Court.

The parties have parted their ways and filed a memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of the CPC r/w. Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005, before the family Court, by drawing up certain terms and conditions.
One of the conditions of the settlement also recognizes the closure of the present proceedings.
An application under Section 320(2) of the Cr.P.C. along with an affidavit is also filed before this Court.

The memorandum of settlement reads as follows:
"11.

In view of the aforesaid settlement the parties shall co-operate / closure / quash /
withdraw the below stated cases:
i.
The respondent agreed to co-operate for closure / quashing of the CC 7/2021 - Vidyaranyapura Police Station.

ii. Parties to file joint memo before the Hon'ble High Court and seek quashing of proceedings before the Magistrate Court and stayed by the Hon'ble High Court in Criminal Petition Nos.6542/2019 and 7057/2022.

Santosh Kumar M vs State Of Karnataka on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139199928/
4 iii.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent to withdraw W.P. 21267/2021 pending before the Hon'ble High Court.
iv. The respondent to withdraw MC  No.2380/2023 and EX.P.No.65/2023  before the II Addl. FC  v. Divorce by mutual consent and  withdrawal of MC 2394/2020, GWC  132/2020 and GWX 54/2021."

Though the offences are alleged against each other in both the petitions, since it is a marital dispute between the husband and wife and family members, and now, they have arrived at settlement and parted their ways, I deem it appropriate to accept the memorandum of understanding and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.

At this juncture, learned counsel for respondent No.2 - complainant would submit that though the settlement is arrived at, there is grievance in respect of the passport of the child, which is in the custody of the husband.
5.

Learned counsel for petitioners submits that the passport of the child is expired three years ago,
when the child was 5 years old and is now 8 years.

6. In the light of the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for both the parties, respondent No.2 - complainant - mother under whose custody the child is, it is open for her to apply for re-issuance of the passport in accordance with law.

7. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The criminal petitions are disposed.
(ii) I.A.No.1/2024 filed in Crl.P.No.7057/2024 seeking compounding of the offences is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC:36744 (iii) The impugned crime No.36/2019, pending before the 43rd Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru,
in Crl.P.No.6542/2019 stands quashed.
